Scottish
aquatech company Aqura Systems has raised £2.1 million in a funding round led
by Archangels alongside Scottish Enterprise to advance its AI-powered robotic
monitoring platform for fish farms. The company has also appointed Norwegian
salmon farming industry veteran Charles Høstlund as chair as it prepares for
international commercialisation.

Founded
by Chris Hyde, Steve Ball and Gareth Hammond, Aqura Systems develops automated
monitoring technology designed to improve fish health and operational
efficiency.

Fish
farmers currently rely on manual sampling and microscope-based analysis to
identify microorganism-related threats. These processes are often
time-consuming, infrequent and inaccurate, making it difficult for farmers to
detect emerging risks and respond before they affect fish health.

Aqura
aims to address these challenges through MIAbot, a fully automated robotic
platform that provides real-time monitoring of biological threats at different
depths and across multiple locations within a fish farm.

The
platform combines a proprietary imaging system with Aqura’s AI engine to
identify microorganisms at the species level, measure their concentrations and
collect depth and other relevant water quality data. The technology currently
focuses on phytoplankton responsible for algal blooms, with monitoring
capabilities for micro jellyfish, sea lice and amoebae also in development.

By
providing continuous access to this information, MIAbot enables farmers to take
preventative action rather than respond to problems after they arise. Pilot
projects are already underway with major salmon farming companies in Scotland.

Chris
Hyde, CEO of Aqura Systems, said:

The
early reception and testing of MIAbot with industry has been very positive.
Globally, aquaculture is a £371 billion industry, but many of its processes are
still manual, so there’s a huge opportunity to harness technology to improve
fish health and increase efficiencies.

The
new funding will enable Aqura Systems to expand its existing AI training
datasets, conduct further testing and refine its technology as it prepares for
commercial deployment and international expansion.
